learning_outcomes.text: Applies theoretical and practical knowledge to model and solve engineering problems in the field of digital electronics (logic circuits).
Identifies, defines, formulates, and solves complex engineering problems encountered in the field of digital electronics by selecting appropriate analysis and modeling methods.
Designs a complex system or process encountered in the field of digital electronics using modern design methods under realistic constraints and conditions.
Develops, selects, and uses modern techniques and tools for digital electronic applications by effectively utilizing information technologies.
Collects data for the examination of engineering problems in the field of digital electronics; analyzes and interprets the results.

syllabus_topics: Binary, octal, and hexadecimal number systems, conversions between number systems, and complement representation.
BCD, ASCII, Excess-3, and Gray Code encoding systems.
Boolean algebra theory, properties, representation forms of Boolean expressions.
Digital logic gates.
Simplification of Boolean functions.
Combinational circuit design.
Sequential logic circuit design with flip-flops, registers, counters, and memory units.
Analog and digital concepts, number systems, binary codes.
Boolean algebra, digital logic gates, integrated circuits, circuits.
Simplification of Boolean functions: Karnaugh maps, tabular (Quine McCluskey) and Petrick method.
Analysis and design of combinational circuits: Mathematical operation circuits.
Analysis and design of combinational circuits: Comparison circuits, decoders, encoders.
Analysis and design of combinational circuits: Multiplexer, data distributor, programmable structures.
Analysis and design of sequential circuits: Flip-flops and application circuits.
Analysis and design of sequential circuits: Flip-flops and application circuits.
Analysis and design of synchronous circuits: Mealy model.
Analysis and design of synchronous circuits: Moore model.
Registers and memories.
Analysis and design of synchronous circuits: Synchronous counters.
Analysis and design of synchronous circuits: Asynchronous counters.
Algorithmic state machines
assessment_rules: The midterm exam contributes 40% and the final exam contributes 60% to the overall grade. Midterm and final exam dates are determined by the University Senate and specified in the academic calendar.
